purpose: Phase 0 machine-readable preservation inventory; seed specification for later migration fixtures and cross-client comparisons.

existingFixtureCoverage.limitation: SyncContractFixturesTest currently contains only a disabled-tests marker; these resources do not cover the full preservation inventory.

assertions.statement: Context stable IDs, names, descriptions, primary parents, secondary parent links, ordering, and tombstones survive migration.
Context roleCode, tags, related links, lifecycle/management fields, scoring inputs and calculated values remain recoverable without changed meaning.
A Context currently used as a semantic domain remains navigable and retains all attached content even if later classified as or related to an Aspect.
ADDITIVE capability resolution preserves role defaults, explicit legacy overrides, and experimental capability IDs.
OVERRIDE capability resolution does not reintroduce role defaults.
A configuration with no preset or overrides retains the compatibility dashboard default, and legacy attachments remains compatible with connections.
Backlog, inbox, direction, log, journal log, key problems, sorting, artifacts, connections and their payloads remain addressable and correctly owned.
Every supported heterogeneous backlog itemType resolves to the same content identity after migration.
The same semantic content placed in multiple Context backlogs retains distinct placement IDs, association metadata, deletion state and per-list order.
BacklogOrder orderVersion and special merge semantics are preserved independently from content and placement versions.
Main Beacon identity and all strategic narrative, readiness, blocker, next-action, ordering and expansion fields survive.
Main Beacon Group identity, title, description, order and ordered memberships survive independently from member Beacons.
Beacon parent graph, Context links, Attachment links and per-level statuses preserve endpoints, order and current authoritative-set/composite semantics.
Goal title, description, status, completion, tags, links, importance, impact, scoring, relative size and cost fields survive with original meaning.
Direction item identity, Context placement, content, order, version and tombstone survive.
Manual Arc Quest remains its own identity; source-backed Arc Quest preserves its source identity and does not become a duplicate canonical semantic object.
ThemeDefinition remains reusable and distinct from its dated DayTheme assignment, budget, order and active state.
Tactical Mission generated Long identity remains resolvable through any future canonical identity mapping.
Every MissionSourceType retains source Context/backlog/ArcQuest/carry-forward provenance as applicable.
Mission status, priority, deadline, week, iteration, stream, activity slot, Context links, attachments and all ordering dimensions survive.
Day Plan identity, date, state, reflection, linked entities and aggregate fields survive.
Day Focus and Responsibility retain type, budget, notes, links, order and recurrence provenance.
Day Task retains Goal, Context, Activity, recurrence, task source, scheduling, status, priority, scoring copies, tags and attachments.
Legacy day-theme payload and canonical theme payload preserve absent-versus-empty semantics through import and sync.
An ongoing activity remains one record with startTime set and endTime null; completing it updates that identity rather than duplicating it.
Activity kind, notes, timestamps, reminder, target, multiple entity links and legacy Goal/Context compatibility fields survive.
Daily metrics, focus Context intervals and user-state intervals remain usable by reflection with current Android ownership.
Deleted versioned rows remain tombstoned and cannot be resurrected by an older snapshot or legacy projection.
Orphan-like rows accepted by current storage are reported and preserved or quarantined; they are never silently dropped or guessed into a relation.
Authoritative-set relations, local composite relations and versioned tombstones retain their distinct deletion semantics until explicit cutover.
Existing Context detail arguments and highlight/deep-link behavior resolve to the same visible subject.
Main Beacon/Core, Strategic, Tactical, Day, Journal and Reflection destinations remain reachable from their existing entry points.
Every added canonical collection declares Desktop ownership, receive strategy and push scope in the same phase.
Existing aliases and collection-specific ownership remain unchanged until an explicit cutover with comparison and repair rules.
Snapshot round-trip preserves canonical day-theme null-versus-empty presence semantics and all tombstone/version metadata.
